items.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had another great director, Danny Mann, who would give me a direction.

ctx.x: Did you feel at any point that your background in theater and on stage became a part of the stage persona and presence that you have?

All of it contributes to the work that I have, experience as an actress or an actor. I don't mind being called an actor. Michael Romer, who was my first serious film, dramatic film, and he made me know, he made me think that I was really a talented and a great actress, and I took his direction, and then I had a chance to make "For Love of Ivy," and I had another great director, Danny Mann, who would give me a direction. I was fortunate. Those are the only two really films I made. "For Love of Ivy." "Nothing But A…
Where do the hats come from?
